A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KL-geodesics flow matching work and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original text-generation and code-infilling experiments in Tables 1–4, plus HumanEval evaluation and sampling/training analyses in Appendices A–D.

after.justification: v4 retains the original experimental results in Tables 1–4 and the additional empirical evaluations and analyses in Appendices A–D.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same logit interpolation, marginal denoising objective, and basic, semi-sampling, sampling, and hybrid inference procedures. Algorithms 1–2 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same TinyStories, Fine Fine Web, Lamini Instruction, WMT14 de-en, and Python-code/MBPP coverage. TinyCodes training and prompted HumanEval code infilling already appear in Appendix A of v2.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–4, including the autoregressive and DFM comparisons and both DFM iteration configurations for MBPP. Appendix A retains the same LFM-versus-DFM comparison.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A retain identical model sizes, sequence lengths, inference budgets, masking procedures, training settings, and evaluation metrics. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: Appendices A–D retain the same masking-rate evaluation, top-k sensitivity study, learning-rate/optimizer and time-conditioning comparisons, and hybrid-threshold sweeps shown in Figures 2–7.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point estimates and plotted curves. Neither reports training-seed or repeated-training run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests; uncertainty reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and Figures 2–7 retain identical results. For example, Table 2 reports Llama 2 perplexity 32.7 for the 1.5B KL-flow hybrid at 1024 NFE in both versions, and Table 4 retains KL-flow sampling Pass@1 of 45.9.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1, Propositions 3.2 and 3.4, Corollary 3.3, their proofs, and Equations 1–24 are unchanged. The proof text shifts across pages without mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims concerning KL-geodesic interpolation, the likelihood/flow-velocity connection, and the empirical advantages of sampling and hybrid inference.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the sampling independence approximation, incomplete theoretical justification, entropy tradeoff, and computational limitation to 1.5B models. Interpretations of when hybrid versus sampling inference works best are unchanged.

D1.justification: Architecture descriptions, smoothing coefficient beta = 0.01, two 80GB H100 GPUs, and the implementation/training details in Section 5 and Appendices A and C are unchanged. The code and data link targets also match.

R1.justification: Section 4, Appendix E, and the bibliography retain the same cited works and research positioning. Changed citation back-reference page numbers reflect pagination only.

P1.justification: v4 adds Nikita Dragunov and an AIRI affiliation to the author block and updates the arXiv version/date header. Scientific prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded author block changes the first-page layout, including the abstract's column break, and introductory/proof text shifts across pages. Conclusion and reference text also reflows, while all four tables and seven figures retain their displays and captions.

improvement.justification: v4 changes authorship information and makes limited layout adjustments while preserving the scientific and explanatory content, including Tables 1–4 and Appendices A–E. No methodological correction, additional evidence, or reproducibility improvement establishes a meaningful overall quality difference.
